capabilities: Sync Jira issues both ways between Jira and note content
Map Jira and custom fields using templates with hidden markers and JavaScript transforms
Transition issues through Jira workflows from Obsidian
Track and batch-submit worklogs in Timekeep or Super Simple Time Tracker formats
Search issues with JQL and add inline comments
extras: Full documentation is hosted elsewhere (separate English and Russian guides plus template examples), not in the README itself. Multiple authentication methods and multiple Jira connections are supported.
intentEvidence: Most Jira plugins for Obsidian treat issues as read-only. This one is built for people who want to work in Obsidian and push changes back
motivation: The author built it because most Jira plugins treat issues as read-only, while they wanted to work in Obsidian and push changes back to Jira.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in Jira integration, and existing Jira plugins only display issues read-only instead of syncing edits back.

relations.evidence: Supports Timekeep and Super Simple Time Tracker formats
Supports Timekeep and Super Simple Time Tracker formats

requires.name: Jira authentication (Bearer Token, Basic Auth, or Session Cookie)

summary: Two-way Jira sync plugin that fetches issues into notes, pushes edits back, and manages statuses, comments and worklogs.
